title: Integral neighbourhood at a normal point of a reduced birational source
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], let $f:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes with $Y$ reduced [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-reduced-scheme], and let $x\in X$ have normal local ring $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Assume $f$ is birational. Birational means that $f$ maps the generic points of the irreducible components of $Y$ bijectively onto those of $X$ and induces isomorphisms $\mathcal O_{X,f(\eta)}\to\mathcal O_{Y,\eta}$ at all these points [def-sc-generic-point, def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. There is an affine open neighbourhood $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $x$ such that the germ map $A\to R$ is injective and both $V$ and $f^{-1}(V)$ are integral schemes [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. The restricted morphism is birational in the same sense.

source.place: Tag 0BFP, lemma-modification-normal-iso-over-codimension-1, first paragraph of proof (4); Properties Tag 0BX3 (lemma-ring-affine-open-injective-local-ring).

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-noetherian-injective-germ-neighbourhood], choose an affine open $x\in V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with injective germ map $A\to R$. The normal local ring $R$ is a domain: in [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], take its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$; $R_{\mathfrak m}$ is a normal domain, and $R\to R_{\mathfrak m}$ is an isomorphism since every denominator outside $\mathfrak m$ is already a unit. Injectivity then makes $A$ a domain (if $ab=0$, one image is zero, hence one factor is zero; $1\ne0$ follows from the unital injection). By clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field], $V$ is integral.

source.place: Tag 0BFP, lemma-modification-normal-iso-over-codimension-1, proof (4), first paragraph; expanded component argument.

proof.text: By [def-pc-integral-scheme], $V$ is nonempty and irreducible. Apply [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover] to $x\in X$. A component $C$ meeting $V$ restricts to a component $C\cap V$ of $V$, and these restrictions are injective in $C$, by [lem-sc-components-open-injection]. Since the only component of the irreducible space $V$ is $V$, precisely one component $C_0$ of $X$ meets $V$. By [lem-sc-scheme-sober], it has a unique generic point $\xi$. This point belongs to $V$: any open meeting $\overline{\{\xi\}}$ contains $\xi$, directly from the definition of closure. Thus $\overline{\{\xi\}}\cap V=C_0\cap V=V$, so $\xi$ is the generic point of $V$. Birationality of $f$ supplies exactly one component-generic point $\eta_0$ of $Y$ with $f(\eta_0)=\xi$. In particular $W=f^{-1}(V)$ is nonempty.

source.place: Tag 0BFP, lemma-modification-normal-iso-over-codimension-1, proof (4), first paragraph; expanded component argument.

proof.text: For any $y\in W$, [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover] puts $y$ in a component $D$ of $Y$, and [lem-sc-scheme-sober] gives its generic point $\eta_D$. Since $W$ is open and $y\in\overline{\{\eta_D\}}$, the closure argument of Step 2 gives $\eta_D\in W$. Birationality says $f(\eta_D)$ is a component-generic point of $X$. Its component meets $V$, hence is $C_0$; sobriety identifies $f(\eta_D)=\xi$. The injectivity on component-generic points in the hypothesis gives $\eta_D=\eta_0$. Consequently every $y\in W$ lies in $\overline{\{\eta_0\}}\cap W$, which is exactly the closure of $\{\eta_0\}$ in $W$. Hence $W$ is irreducible: if $W=F\cup G$ with $F,G$ closed, the one containing $\eta_0$ contains its closure and equals $W$.

source.place: Tag 0BFP, lemma-modification-normal-iso-over-codimension-1, proof (4), first paragraph; expanded component argument.

proof.text: The open subscheme $W$ is reduced by [def-pc-reduced-scheme] and [def-weil-open-immersion]: at $y\in W$ its local ring is $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$. This stalk identification follows directly from germs [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], since the neighbourhoods contained in the open $W$ are cofinal among all neighbourhoods of $y$. By [def-pc-integral-scheme], the nonempty reduced irreducible scheme $W$ is integral. The same open-stalk identification for $V\subseteq X$ identifies the restricted stalk map at $\eta_0$ with $\mathcal O_{X,\xi}\to\mathcal O_{Y,\eta_0}$, which is an isomorphism by the birational hypothesis. The two integral schemes have the unique generic points $\eta_0$ and $\xi$, and the restriction maps the former to the latter. This proves its birationality and all the asserted conclusions.

lean.statement: theorem exists_integral_affine_neighbourhood_of_birational_normal_stalk {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (f : Y ⟶ X) [IsReduced Y] (x : X) (hnormal : ∀ (p : Ideal (X.presheaf.stalk x)) [p.IsPrime], IsDomain (Localization.AtPrime p) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (Localization.AtPrime p)) (hgeneric : Set.BijOn f (genericPoints Y) (genericPoints X)) (hstalk : ∀ η : Y, η ∈ genericPoints Y → IsIso (f.stalkMap η)) : ∃ (V : X.Opens) (hxV : x ∈ V), IsAffineOpen V ∧ Function.Injective (X.presheaf.germ V x hxV) ∧ IsIntegral V.toScheme ∧ IsIntegral (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).toScheme ∧ Set.BijOn (f ∣_ V) (genericPoints (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).toScheme) (genericPoints V.toScheme) ∧ ∀ η : (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).toScheme, η ∈ genericPoints (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).toScheme → IsIso ((f ∣_ V).stalkMap η)
